Commentary.Commentary: Right then, with that, we wrap up this final warm-up game ahead of the main league stage of the T20 World Cup 2024. India clinches a commanding victory over Bangladesh. India will now gear up to take on Ireland to commence their mission of winning the trophy, while Bangladesh will look forward to kickstart its campaign against Sri Lanka later next week. The commencement of the league stage is just a few hours away from now, as the hosts USA are all set to begin their campaign against their northern neighbors, Canada in the inaugural game of the league phase. The match is scheduled to start on June 2nd, Sunday with the first ball set to be bowled at 6 am IST (12:30 am GMT). Do join us for the pre-match build-up. Till then, cheers and take care!

Earlier in the game, India chose to bat first but struggled initially as the batters adjusted to the new conditions of New York. Sanju Samson couldn't hold on and was dismissed early. Rohit Sharma also fell after a promising start. Rishabh Pant and Suryakumar Yadav then formed a responsible partnership, with Pant taking charge and accelerating the innings beautifully to score a brilliant fifty, while Yadav also contributed with a quick 31. After SKY's departure, Hardik Pandya came in all guns blazing and played a magnificent clutch inning in the backend smashing 40 off just 23. In the chase, Bangladesh couldn't gain any momentum and lost wickets at regular intervals. The Indian bowlers severely disrupted their batting order. However, Mahmudullah and Shakib Al Hasan formed a crucial partnership but Bangladesh was way too behind in the game by then.

India, on the other hand, began strongly with the ball. Arshdeep Singh struck in his first over, posing tough questions with conventional Test-match lengths and good swing. Jasprit Bumrah bowled with precision, keeping the Bangladeshi batters in check. Mohammed Siraj then claimed a wicket by hitting the deck hard and capitalizing on the pitch's assistance. Arshdeep removed Litton Das with a stunning delivery, helping India take control of the game. Hardik Pandya and Axar Patel then each claimed a wicket in quick succession and dented the middle order of Bangladesh badly. The spinners, Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav, may not have taken wickets, but they effectively compounded the pressure with their economical spells. Hardik Pandya got a wicket to his name whereas Shivam Dube came in as a surprise package in the backend picking up two to his name which led India to a dominating victory over their sub-continental counterparts.

India win by a comfortable margin of 60 runs in this final warm-up game of this ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024. Bangladesh struggled from the start, unable to handle the ball's early movement. The ball repeatedly beat their outside edges, with Soumya Sarkar falling in the first over and Litton Das following soon after. Najmul Hossain Shanto's dismissal left Bangladesh in tatters as they limped through the Powerplay. Towhid Hridoy's brief and struggling stay at the crease also came to an end as he departed for 13. Tanzid Hasan couldn't sustain as well and threw his wicket away under pressure. Bangladesh lost half of its side below 50. The veteran duo of Shakib Al Hasan and Mahmudullah then formed a resilient partnership, but Bangladesh was already too far behind. Despite this, they managed to keep the scoreboard ticking. The two complemented each other well, putting together crucial runs and showcasing all their experience. But in the end, they badly collapsed and faced a thumping defeat.
Done and dusted! India crushes Bangladesh in its solitary warm-up game. Back of a length, outside the off stump, Mahedi Hasan hits it with a cross bat to long off for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Towhid Hridoy is the next man in.

OUT! TAKEN! India is in a dominating position with this scalp. Mohammed Siraj gets his first. Bumps into the deck, short and on the top of the middle and off-channel, rises off the deck a bit as well. Najmul Hossain Shanto is a bit late on the pull shot and hits it with no timing off the toe-end of the blade, straight towards mid on where Hardik Pandya takes a good catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Hardik Pandya b Mohammed Siraj
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Mohammed Siraj to Najmul Hossain Shanto, OUT! c Hardik Pandya b Mohammed Siraj.

Commentary.Commentary: Injects a length-delivery swinging minimally into the pads, Najmul Hossain Shanto outside edges to the slip cordon going for a flick shot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Mohammed Siraj to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls a conventional hard length ball, on the middle this time, Najmul Hossain Shanto alertly punches it off the back foot to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Mohammed Siraj to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On the back of a length again, across off, Najmul Hossain Shanto hops back and knocks it solidly off the back foot straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mohammed Siraj to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Over the wicket, on the back of a length around off, Tanzid Hasan stays leg side of the ball, watches closely and cuts it late through backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mohammed Siraj to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches on off, good length, Tanzid Hasan pulls it from the top half of the bat in front of mid on and runs a quick single to end the over.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, aims the off stump, Tanzid Hasan gets in line of the ball, and solidly punches it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arshdeep Singh to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Again a good away swinger on a hard length, outside off, Tanzid Hasan swings across and misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arshdeep Singh to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angles it into the batter on a hard length, Najmul Hossain Shanto skips ahead and weirdly tries to pull it away and gets no connection on the shot at all as he plays it too close to the body. The ball hits his chest and rolls to the square leg region. A leg bye taken though.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Attacks the stumps on a length, Najmul Hossain Shanto hops on the back foot and punches it down to the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Najmul Hossain Shanto comes out to the middle now.

OUT! KNOCKED HIM OVER! Arshdeep Singh gets his second wicket and in what style! Steams in from over the wicket, lands it on a good length, on the off stump line and gets it to swing into the batter. Litton Das totally gets deceived by the inswinger and is cramped up for room. The ball sneaks through the gap between the pad and the bat and disrupts the furniture. Bangladesh in a huge trouble first up.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arshdeep Singh to Litton Das, OUT! b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: A knee-length full toss on off, Tanzid Hasan knocks it straight to covers to end the over. Absolute ripper of an over from Jasprit Bumrah.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Jasprit Bumrah to Tanzid Hasan, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length again, outside off, Litton Das with no real timing drives it on the up for a single at widish cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Jasprit Bumrah to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the deck hard, and keeps it outside off, Litton Das lets it go this time.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Jasprit Bumrah to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely played! Bowls it full and on the middle, Litton Das shuffles a bit across off and flicks it nicely with his wrists over square leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Jasprit Bumrah to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten again! On the fourth stump line, on a length, Litton Das goes for a poke again and gets beaten on the outside edge. Rishabh Pant bends low to collect it on the knee length.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Jasprit Bumrah to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: To the point! Hard length, just in the corridor of uncertainty around off, nips away a shade, Litton Das gets beaten on the outside edge as he goes for a front foot defence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Jasprit Bumrah to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Jasprit Bumrah to share the attack.

An excellent over from Arshdeep Singh! Nails a yoker on off, Litton Das just jams the bat down in time and hits it in front of mid off for a quick single to end the first over. A successful one for India.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arshdeep Singh to Litton Das, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it outside off, and gets it to swing in a bit, on a fuller length, Litton Das presents full face of the willow and drives it to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arshdeep Singh to Litton Das, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Litton Das walks out to bat number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Arshdeep Singh strikes and India get the first wicket in the very first over. Holds onto that typical test match length, full and swings away from off neatly, Soumya Sarkar goes for a drive through the covers but again plays inside the line of the ball and it takes the faint outside edge of the blade. The ball carries well into the keeper's gloves and Rishabh Pant takes a regulation grab behind the wicket. Arshdeep Singh and India couldn't have asked for a better start here.
Commentary.Howout: c Rishabh Pant b Arshdeep Singh
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arshdeep Singh to Soumya Sarkar, OUT! c Rishabh Pant b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! This is pitched up, on the off stump line, with a dramatic outswing again, Soumya Sarkar goes for a front foot defence but plays inside the line of the ball and gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arshdeep Singh to Soumya Sarkar, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it closer to the body now, on a hard length with a bit of an away movement, Tanzid Hasan pats it off the back foot through gully for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arshdeep Singh to Tanzid Hasan, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: BEATEN! A screamer of a delivery first up from Arshdeep Singh! Swings it away from off on a length, Tanzid Hasan gets beaten on the outside edge.
